target_customer: Hardware companies in the San Francisco Bay Area that need small batches of machined parts quickly
problem: Prototype and low volume CNC parts take long to quote and make, and each new design needs manual setup.
business_model: On-demand CNC parts service with instant software quoting, aiming to become manufacturing as an API

founders.name: Hemant Mahendru
founders.background_notes: YC page says he built ATVs, ran supersonic simulations and designed products for high volume manufacturing.

founders.name: Sam Mathew
previous_startups: First company sold at 18 (name not given)
founders.background_notes: YC page says about a decade building hardware and software, then two years with vertical AI agent startups.

competitors.name: Xometry
competitors.traction_then: listed as a leading platform in 2026 comparisons

competitors.name: Protolabs (with Hubs)
competitors.what: Digital CNC manufacturing with quick turn
competitors.traction_then: five to ten business day small quantity delivery per a 2026 guide

competitors.name: Fictiv
competitors.what: Manufacturing platform that added AI instant quoting and auto DFM in 2025 per a vendor blog

technical_complexity.rationale: Standardized machining cells plus models that read CAD and plan toolpaths, setups and workholding is hard automation, though the first product is a human run shop with a quoting tool.

defensibility.rationale: Own machines generate production data, but quoting and shop services are widely offered and funded competitors already exist.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents already offer AI quoting; funded AI manufacturing startups such as CloudNC, Limitless Labs and SAEKI raised rounds in 2026 per search results.

market_need_then: Hardware startups need fast machined parts. The company says it already makes parts for Bay Area hardware firms with turnaround near 48 hours.

identity.logo: present on YC page, not described
identity.voice_and_tone: Founder letter on the site in first person, hands on shop tone

branding.community_and_virality: A Fondo interview with Sam Mathew dated 2026-09-22; no other brand coverage found.

brand_strength.rationale: A brand search found nothing about the name or logo. The name mixes words and digits, so it is hard to say or recall.

pivots.to: Operating an on-demand CNC machine shop
pivots.why: Per a Fondo interview summary, they moved from building software to machining so automation could be built on real production work

outcome_analysis: twentyfour26 is a Fall 2026 YC company with two founders and an operating shop, so it is far too early for an outcome. Competition from funded AI manufacturing firms is heavy, and the pivot from software to a shop is a capital intensive path.
